title: Tool call visualization

key_findings.title: Correct UI Implementation, Missed Producer Update
key_findings.description: Code-writer correctly implemented the ToolCallDisplay component with all AC requirements. However, when adding startedAt/completedAt timestamp fields to the toolCalls type interface, the WebSocket stream handler (use-agent-stream.ts) was not updated to stamp the timestamps. This was caught by Gate B code review and fixed in 1 cycle.
key_findings.lesson: Type system changes have a producer-consumer relationship across layers: shared types → database schema → API producers → UI consumers. All must be kept in sync. Missing a producer causes undefined values in consumers.

key_findings.title: Low Risk, Efficient Implementation
key_findings.description: 30-minute execution with single iteration indicates good planning and understanding of requirements. Risk was correctly assessed as LOW in Phase 1.

key_findings.title: Strong Test Coverage First Try
key_findings.description: 32 tests passed on first try across 2 new test files (tool-categories.test.ts, tool-call-display.test.tsx). All 4 acceptance criteria have corresponding test cases.

patterns_extracted.name: TYPE_SYSTEM_PRODUCER_CONSUMER_SYNC
patterns_extracted.recommendation: When modifying type definitions, create a checklist: 1) Shared types package, 2) Database schema, 3) ALL producers (handlers, mutations, API), 4) ALL consumers (UI, display), 5) Tests. Update in dependency order and run integration tests.

lines_of_code.distribution: Well distributed across utilities (100+), components (150+), types (50+), schema (50+), tests (52)

code_review.critical_issue: Missing timestamp stamping in use-agent-stream.ts. When tool calls are received via WebSocket, startedAt/completedAt should be stamped by the handler before being stored in state.
code_review.fix_applied: Added timestamp stamping logic to WebSocket message handler

security_review.summary: No security concerns. Color-coded badges are CSS-only, file diffs use existing sanitized DiffViewer component.

future_improvement_opportunities: Consider adding e2e test with mock WebSocket stream to verify timestamp stamping end-to-end
Add performance profile for DiffViewer with large file diffs (consider virtualization if >1000 lines)
Document tool type categories as config file (tool-categories.config.ts) for easier extension
retrospective: F037 demonstrates the value of code review catching integration issues. The code-writer implemented the UI layer correctly and completely, but missed the producer update in the data flow. This is a common pattern in distributed type system changes. With PAT-017 documented and added to future review checklists, similar issues can be caught earlier in development. The single-iteration success and strong test coverage (32 tests) show excellent understanding of requirements.
